claims.text: Hybrid thermodynamic integration combined with metadynamics or replica exchange can accurately predict melting temperatures across a wide range of high-entropy alloy compositions.
The proposed framework can accurately predict enthalpies and entropies of fusion across a wide range of high-entropy alloy compositions.
The proposed framework can accurately predict volume changes at melting across a wide range of high-entropy alloy compositions.
The proposed framework can reliably predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The proposed framework is computationally efficient for surveying a wide range of high-entropy alloy compositions.
High-entropy alloys near melting exhibit multi-principal-element disorder.
Enhanced sampling can overcome free-energy sampling barriers inherent in disordered multicomponent systems.
The enhanced-sampling framework can directly map the free-energy difference between solid and liquid phases.
Accurately capturing small solid-liquid free-energy differences and latent heat enables quantitative prediction of fusion properties.
Combining thermodynamic integration with enhanced sampling reduces systematic errors relative to conventional molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo, or CALPHAD methods.
Predicted melting temperatures, fusion enthalpies, fusion entropies, and melting volume changes are expected to agree with experiments within approximately 5%.
Traditional calorimetry lacks the throughput needed to scan the large high-entropy-alloy composition space rapidly.
Standard atomistic simulations have insufficient accuracy for resolving fine free-energy differences in highly disordered alloys.
Extremely nonlinear compositions may cause the method to exceed its 5% accuracy target.
Exceptionally pronounced dynamic anharmonicity near melting may cause the method to exceed its 5% accuracy target.
Extreme compositional disorder may create substantial computational-cost and convergence problems.
